key_insight: Brief speech narratives combined with linguistic AI features showed potential for education-calibrated developmental monitoring and mental health screening.
clinical_relevance: Speech-based models may support assessment of psychosis, depression, and anxiety symptoms, but these findings do not establish a standalone diagnostic tool.
method: Derived narrative complexity and emotional narrative complexity indices from picture-elicited speech.
Built schooling-calibrated normative curves using 2,149 participants.
Combined graph-derived, psycholinguistic, and emotional features in machine-learning models.
evidence_signal: In a 120-person transdiagnostic sample, expanded classifiers achieved AUCs of 0.774 for symptom risk and 0.858 for diagnosis; symptom-severity models reported AUCs of 0.74–0.92 with sensitivity ≥0.80.
watch_item: Emotional narrative complexity alone did not distinguish groups, and the abstract does not report external validation of the models.
paper_title: SPEECH FEATURES IN A DEVELOPMENTAL PERSPECTIVE: A SCREENING TOOL FOR PSYCHOSIS, DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY
